original_query:
User environment variables no longer getting picked up after upgrade to 4.1.1.1 or 4.1.1.2?
Have you found that after upgrade to Streams 4.1.1.1 or 4.1.1.2, that environment variables set in your .bashrc are no longer being set? For example ODBCINI is not set for the database toolkit and you get

     An SQL operation failed. The SQL state is 08003, the SQL code
     is 0 and the SQL message is [unixODBC][Driver
     Manager]Connnection does not exist.

chunk.text:
IBM STREAMS 4.1.1.1 and 4.1.1.2  JOBS DO NOT INHERIT THE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES SET IN .BASHRC, WHEN STREAMS IS RUN AS A SYSTEM SERVICE - United States

FLASH (ALERT)

ABSTRACT
 In Streams 4.1.1.1 and 4.1.1.2 Streams jobs may not pick up the user enviroment from the streams user's .bashrc. This behavior is different from earlier releases. With these versions, when Streams is run as a system service, application environment variables must be set with streamtool. 

CONTENT
Problem Description
When running Streams as a system service with Streams releases 4.1.1.1
or 4.1.1.2, toolkits and user applications that depend on the
user environment may have various errors.
For example the database toolkit might show the following error
if it does not pick up the ODBCINI environment variable:



 * "An SQL operation failed. The SQL state is 08003, the SQL code
   is 0 and the SQL message is [unixODBC][Driver
   Manager]Connnection does not exist."
 * 

Problem Solution

IBM Environment Variables gone after bash update - United States

BASH C:D Connect:Direct UNIX LINUX environment variables poodle fix TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Since applying a fix to BASH on a Linux host, in response to the POODLE vulnerability, it is no longer possible to access or use inherited environment variables that used to work fine within IBM Sterling Connect:Direct for Unix RUN TASKs. Why? 

CAUSE
A flaw was found in the way BASH evaluated certain specially crafted environment variables. An attacker could use this flaw to override or bypass environment restrictions to execute shell commands. Certain services and applications allow remote unauthenticated attackers to provide environment variables, allowing them to exploit this issue. 

ANSWER
In response to this weakness, and to close the door on this vulnerability, BASH was fixed to restrict the ability to use inherited environmental variables.

IBM For Linux platform, environment variables and libraries are missing for IBM Cognos Data Manager on the developer systems - United States

RN1.0; SRX; RATLC01525037 TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 If Rational Insight server is not installed on a developer system running on Linux, the required environment variables and libraries need to be set up so that IBM Cognos Data Manager (DM) work properly. 

SYMPTOM
When installing Data Manager (DM) on Linux without the Insight reporting server component, such as when installing on a developer's machine, there are missing environment variables and libraries that need to be setup for DM to function properly.

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Follow these steps: 

1. Add the following commands to the profile of the user account; for example, .bashrc

export PATH="<Rational Insight installation directory>/cognos/bin:$PATH" 

export COG_ROOT="<Rational Insight installation directory>/cognos" 

export JAVA_HOME="<Rational Insight installation directory>/dataconfig/jdk/jre" 

export LD_PRELOAD="/usr/lib/libfreetype.so $LD_PRELOAD"

IBM IC88131: INCORRECT DOCUMENTATION FOR DATABASE TOOLKIT ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES - United States

APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS FIXED IF NEXT.
    
   
   

ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  The InfoSphere Streams Version 2.0 documentation contains a
   topic called "How to use the Database Toolkit":
   http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/streams/v2r0/topic/com. [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/streams/v2r0/topic/com.]
   ibm.swg.im.infosphere.streams.database-toolkit.doc/doc/howtouset
   hedatabasetoolkit.html
   
   It contains the following information:
   "...In addition to assigning some value to exactly one of the
   environment variables listed above, you must set the environment
   variables STREAMS_ADAPTERS_ODBC_INCPATH and
   STREAMS_ADAPTERS_ODBC_LIBPATH to the installed directory
   locations of the header files and the libraries for the database
   product that you are using....".
   
   This is incorrect.  You must set those environment variables to
   the location of the include and library directories for the ODBC
   driver that you are using.
   
   
    
   
   

LOCAL FIX

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  Documentation will be fixed in 3.0

CAUSE
Environment Variables were not configured correctly

ENVIRONMENT

Version: 7.3
Database: DB2

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Identify the correct variables as per the documentation and update environment variables to allow access for the correct database type.

Also had to configure the COGNOS_HOME variable to point to the correct directory in the environment variables.

Steps:Set environment variables as outlined in attached documentation from Page 56 to Page 60 ( Solution Installation Guide for Unix ) for specified database type.

DG4ODBC is used in UNIX environments to access archived data. This facility requires the use of Optim Connect (Attunity) 5.3.2 or above, and the Optim Connect ODBC 3.5 driver.

IBM Information Server DataStage job aborts with error "Abnormal termination of stage detected" - United States

TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)

PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Information Server DataStage job aborts with error "Abnormal termination of stage detected" 

CAUSE
The DataStage environment has both the environment variables ODBCINST and ODBCINI set to a different directory path

DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
In DataStage Director open the log for the failed job. Double click the log entry that states "Environment variable settings" to view the complete list of variables used by the job and search for the variable ODBCINST. Verify that the variable ODBCINST is defined and that its value is set to a path that is different from the path of the variable ODBCINI 

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
ODBCINST is an environment variable that defines the directory where the odbc.ini file exists when unixODBC drivers are installed.

ANSWER
In response to this weakness, and to close the door on this vulnerability, BASH was fixed to restrict the ability to use inherited environmental variables.

In response to this weakness, and to close the door on this vulnerability, BASH was fixed to restrict the ability to use inherited environmental variables.

IBM Environment Variables gone after bash update - United States

BASH C:D Connect:Direct UNIX LINUX environment variables poodle fix TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 Since applying a fix to BASH on a Linux host, in response to the POODLE vulnerability, it is no longer possible to access or use inherited environment variables that used to work fine within IBM Sterling Connect:Direct for Unix RUN TASKs. Why? 

CAUSE
A flaw was found in the way BASH evaluated certain specially crafted environment variables. An attacker could use this flaw to override or bypass environment restrictions to execute shell commands. Certain services and applications allow remote unauthenticated attackers to provide environment variables, allowing them to exploit this issue. 

ANSWER
In response to this weakness, and to close the door on this vulnerability, BASH was fixed to restrict the ability to use inherited environmental variables.

FLASH (ALERT)

ABSTRACT
 In Streams 4.1.1.1 and 4.1.1.2 Streams jobs may not pick up the user enviroment from the streams user's .bashrc. This behavior is different from earlier releases. With these versions, when Streams is run as a system service, application environment variables must be set with streamtool. 

CONTENT
Problem Description
When running Streams as a system service with Streams releases 4.1.1.1
or 4.1.1.2, toolkits and user applications that depend on the
user environment may have various errors.
For example the database toolkit might show the following error
if it does not pick up the ODBCINI environment variable:



 * "An SQL operation failed. The SQL state is 08003, the SQL code
   is 0 and the SQL message is [unixODBC][Driver
   Manager]Connnection does not exist."
 * 

Problem Solution

chunk.text:
IBM STREAMS 4.1.1.1 and 4.1.1.2  JOBS DO NOT INHERIT THE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES SET IN .BASHRC, WHEN STREAMS IS RUN AS A SYSTEM SERVICE - United States

FLASH (ALERT)

ABSTRACT
 In Streams 4.1.1.1 and 4.1.1.2 Streams jobs may not pick up the user enviroment from the streams user's .bashrc. This behavior is different from earlier releases. With these versions, when Streams is run as a system service, application environment variables must be set with streamtool. 

CONTENT
Problem Description
When running Streams as a system service with Streams releases 4.1.1.1
or 4.1.1.2, toolkits and user applications that depend on the
user environment may have various errors.
For example the database toolkit might show the following error
if it does not pick up the ODBCINI environment variable:



 * "An SQL operation failed. The SQL state is 08003, the SQL code
   is 0 and the SQL message is [unixODBC][Driver
   Manager]Connnection does not exist."
 * 

Problem Solution

FLASH (ALERT)

ABSTRACT
 In Streams 4.1.1.1 and 4.1.1.2 Streams jobs may not pick up the user enviroment from the streams user's .bashrc. This behavior is different from earlier releases. With these versions, when Streams is run as a system service, application environment variables must be set with streamtool. 

CONTENT
Problem Description
When running Streams as a system service with Streams releases 4.1.1.1
or 4.1.1.2, toolkits and user applications that depend on the
user environment may have various errors.
For example the database toolkit might show the following error
if it does not pick up the ODBCINI environment variable:



 * "An SQL operation failed. The SQL state is 08003, the SQL code
   is 0 and the SQL message is [unixODBC][Driver
   Manager]Connnection does not exist."
 * 

Problem Solution 

To work around the issue, set environment variables that are needed by the application directly in the instance with:  * 
   
 * streamtool setproperty
 * -d <domain> -i <instance>
   --application-ev <VARIABLE NAME>=<VARIABLE VALUE>
 *
